issues.body:
With reuseExistingServer:false, a `serve` process orphaned by an interrupted prior run (Ctrl-C that leaves the child alive) will now make every subsequent local `npm test` fail at webServer startup instead of silently reusing it. This is the intended trade-off and the inline comment at lines 91-94 explains the WHY, but gui/e2e-playwright/README.md's "Run it" section documents neither the new failure mode nor its two remedies (kill the stale listener, or set PLAYWRIGHT_PORT). A developer hitting the collision error for the first time has to read the config to learn that PLAYWRIGHT_PORT exists.

Non-blocking: CI is unaffected, and Playwright's own "is already used, make sure that nothing is running on the port" message is reasonably self-explanatory.
issues.fix_hint: Optionally add one line to the "Run it" section of gui/e2e-playwright/README.md, e.g.: "The lane never reuses an existing listener (reuseExistingServer:false) so a stale export from another worktree can't be tested silently. If port 3007 is already held, either free it or run with PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=<n> npm test." No code change needed.
issues.title: Local recovery path (orphaned `serve` on 3007) is undocumented in the lane README

verdict.summary:
One-line config change: gui/e2e-playwright/playwright.config.ts flips webServer.reuseExistingServer from `!process.env.CI` to a constant `false`, with a comment explaining the rationale (a listener on the fixed port 3007 may belong to another worktree and serve a stale gui/app/out export).

Verified against the checkout: (1) CI behavior is UNCHANGED — with CI set, `!process.env.CI` already evaluated to false, and .github/workflows/gui.yml's gui-mock-ipc job runs only `npm test` (no externally pre-started `serve`), so Playwright already owned the server lifecycle there. (2) The escape hatch cited in the comment is real: SERVE_PORT (line 21) is derived from PLAYWRIGHT_PORT and feeds webServer.command, webServer.url, and use.baseURL consistently, so a parallel worktree run on a distinct port still works end-to-end. (3) Playwright's documented semantics for reuseExistingServer:false are to fail with an "already used" error on port collision, which matches the stated intent of failing loudly rather than silently testing a stale export. (4) No spec, fixture, or gate depends on server reuse; support/fixtures.ts and web-fixtures.ts only reference 127.0.0.1:3007 in comments.

No correctness, soundness, or security concern. No tests are added or changed and none are warranted — this is a harness policy knob, not testable logic, so there is no vacuous-test risk. The accepted trade-off is local ergonomics: an orphaned `serve` from an interrupted prior run now blocks subsequent local runs until the developer kills it or sets PLAYWRIGHT_PORT. That is the intended behavior and Playwright's error message is self-explanatory, so it is a nit, not a blocker.

Out of scope but worth noting for a follow-up (not filed as an issue since the file is not in this diff): site/playwright.config.ts:193 still uses `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI` and carries the same stale-server hazard, so the two Playwright lanes are now inconsistent.
